name: Colewort Green
lede: Colewort Green is a greenish grey from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, with a name that is older than the dictionary itself.

sections.title: An old name on a 1930 plate
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places this hue on plate 30, cell H1, but dates the name itself to 1705, far earlier than most of its plate-mates [1]. *Colewort* is an old word for a leafy brassica, a cabbage-family plant, and the dictionary separately lists the same plate cell under Cabbage Green, dated 1789 [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 report files the hue as a greenish grey [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[harbor-rat]], [[titmouse-blue]], [[deep-medici-blue]] and [[concrete-grey]], at 2.5, 4.4, 4.7 and 5 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this muted green-grey in 783 of 23,781 paintings, about 3.3 percent, as photographed [4]. It is strongest in the 1940s decade and in painters such as Armand Guillaumin, Philips Wouwerman and Meindert Hobbema [4]. A grey this close to green often reads as shadow or weathered stone rather than a leaf itself [4]. The count is a computed match, not a pigment identification [4].
